description:
Moves the benchmarks that call `LdpcDecoder::decode_batch` to the batch soft-decoder trait with unchanged workloads.

## Background

The batch soft-decoder trait of `gf2-coding` decodes a batch of LLR frames into caller-provided decoded words and per-frame outcomes in input order. Its LDPC implementer, the LDPC batch decoder, decodes fixed waves of eight lanes with per-frame termination, routes a wave to the lane kernels or to the single-frame decoder by the decode selectors of the coding tuning section, and returns each frame's result equal to the single-frame decoder's bit for bit as `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states. A pooled batch decoder over the trait gives parallel decoding with one inner decoder per worker. `LdpcDecoder::decode_batch` and `decode_batch_with_config` predate the trait: they build one single-frame decoder per frame, on rayon under the `parallel` feature, and return message bits with iteration counts and flags. Their benchmark callers are `quick_parallel`, `allocation_optimization` and `ldpc_throughput` under `crates/gf2-coding/benches/`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each of the three benchmarks decodes through the batch soft-decoder trait with the LDPC batch decoder, pooled where the benchmark measured parallel decoding.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each benchmark keeps its codes, frame counts, iteration caps and group names.
- [hard] REQ-03: The benchmarks build, and no benchmark in `gf2-coding` calls the inherent batch functions.
title: Move the benchmarks of the inherent LDPC batch functions to the batch trait
